audit.whatIsWrong: The two sides of this matchup do not agree on who wins it. packets/cassiopeia.json gives Cassiopeia 64.62% over 65 games; packets/zac.json gives Zac 56.92% over the same 65 games. Both cannot be true.
audit.why: Same sample size, opposite conclusions. The already-audited mirror (audits/top/zac__cassiopeia.json) built its whole difficulty argument on 56.92%, so whichever number is wrong has already propagated into a second page.
audit.corrected: Nothing — I did not touch the win rate on either side. Raised in questionsForUser.

audit.why: The prose arc — even at 1, Cassiopeia's from 2 onward, the danger being the teamfight rather than the lane — is consistent with the mirror's reading that Zac's only route is the engage and Cassiopeia's grounding takes it away. Early, mid, side-lane and teamfight are all covered.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere in either layer; the packet flags this matchup as naming none of Zac's abilities at all.
audit.why: The decisive comparison, already established from the other side of this matchup, is Miasma 24/22/20/18/16s against Elastic Slingshot 21/18/15/12/9s. Your grounding tool is on a longer cooldown than his engage at every rank, so you cannot trade it one-for-one — you hold it. Cell Division's revive is a flat 5 minutes.
audit.corrected: Put both numbers and the hold-do-not-spend conclusion into the cooldown breakdown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three problems. (a) Zac is described entirely as 'his E sling', 'his blob', 'his passive blobs' — no ability is named. (b) Both spikes[1] and whys[4] claim Petrifying Gaze 'stuns him mid-sling'. (c) The passive is described as blobs that 're-merge' to heal him, conflating two separate mechanics.
audit.why: Riot text: Cell Division sheds a reabsorbable chunk on each ability hit, and separately splits him into four bloblets on FATAL damage for the revive. Petrifying Gaze stuns 'enemies in front of her that are facing her' — nothing in Riot's text says it interrupts an airborne dash, and cassiopeia.json's needsResearch is empty, so that is unknown. The mirror audit removed the same claim from Zac's page for exactly this reason; leaving it here would put the two directions in contradiction.
audit.corrected: Named Stretching Strikes, Unstable Matter, Elastic Slingshot and Cell Division; separated the shed chunks from the revive; and replaced 'stun him mid-sling' with the verified facing rule — R him as he turns to fight, not as he flies.

audit.whatIsWrong: Stretching Strikes is treated as a straightforward knock-up in wants.foe[1].
audit.why: Riot text: 'Zac stretches an arm, grabbing an enemy. Attacking a different enemy will cause him to throw both targets towards each other.' Grabbing you alone does nothing until he lands a second target, so a Zac with no minion or ally beside you has half an ability.
audit.corrected: Rewrote the enemy want to state the two-target requirement.

edits.after: Petrifying Gaze punishes his landing: it stuns only what is facing you, so fire it as he turns to fight and your stacked poison melts him before the shed chunks heal him back.

edits.before: Level 1 is the only even patch — you have one ability and no Q poison to feed Twin Fang yet, so don't let an early Q poke or autos chunk you for free; just last-hit and stay healthy. From level 2 you flip it: place Q so the zone poisons him, then E the poisoned cell, and Serpentine Grace's move speed lets you walk out of his slow approach. The thing that loses you the lane is eating a fog E sling before your W is online, so ward the side brush and keep Miasma ready to ground any sling he throws.
edits.after: Level 1 is the only even patch — you have one ability and no Q poison to feed Twin Fang yet, so do not let an early poke or his autos chunk you for free; last-hit and stay healthy. From level 2 you flip it: place Q so the zone poisons him, then Twin Fang the poisoned target, and Serpentine Grace lets you walk out of his slow approach. edits.before: This is your takeover. Ranks in Q and E let you chain near-continuous Twin Fangs — the refund on a poisoned target keeps Twin Fang up — and an immobile blob is exactly what you shred. He has no dash to close once you ground his E with W, so he either walks into your poison or concedes the wave. At 6, hold Petrifying Gaze for his sling: stun him as he lands and your poison eats him before his passive blobs can re-merge. Bait the E engage, ground it, kite back, and DPS him down.
edits.after: This is your takeover. Ranks in Q and E let you chain near-continuous Twin Fang — the refund on a poisoned target keeps it up — and an immobile blob is exactly what you shred. Miasma is 24s at rank 1 against his 21s Elastic Slingshot, so never trade it for chip: hold it, and he either walks into your poison or concedes the wave. At 6, hold Petrifying Gaze for his commit and stun him as he turns to fight, then eat him before the Cell Division chunks bring him back.

edits.before: Poison shreds HP stacking — free DPS lane where only his engage cooldown deserves respect.
edits.after: Poison shreds HP stacking — a free DPS lane where only Elastic Slingshot deserves respect.

edits.before: - Zac Elastic Slingshot: matchup-defining — Long-range engage — interrupt the charge or punish the cooldown. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your W Miasma like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Zac Elastic Slingshot: matchup-defining — 21s at rank 1, and Miasma grounds it. Your W is 24s, so you cannot trade it one-for-one: hold it. - Cell Division's revive is a flat 5 minutes. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.

edits.before: Spamming E without poison until your mana bar dies — and then standing in Elastic Slingshot range with Miasma on cooldown.
edits.after: Spamming E without poison until your mana bar dies — or spending Miasma on chip while Elastic Slingshot is up.

notes: Mirror reused: audits/top/zac__cassiopeia.json was already written, and I took its mechanical findings rather than re-deriving them — the Miasma 24s vs Elastic Slingshot 21s comparison, the Cell Division chunks-versus-revive split, and its deliberate removal of the 'stun him mid-air' claim. I removed that claim from this side too so the two pages agree. One thing the mirror and this side genuinely cannot both be right about: the win rate. packets/cassiopeia.json says Cassiopeia 64.62% and packets/zac.json says Zac 56.92%, both over 65 games. Neither page was edited on that point.
